definition_zh: 职员；店员；办事员；文书
definition_en: a person who works in an office or shop keeping records or serving customers
core_image: 柜台后或办公桌前，一边整理文件一边招呼客人的人
scene: 超市里，收银员正帮妈妈扫码结账。The clerk scanned the food quickly at the supermarket.
sceneCN: 这里 clerk 是「店员」（第 1 个义项：在商店里服务顾客的人）；句意是超市店员麻利地给食物扫码。

derivatives.zh: 由 clerk  + suffix  -ship 构成，义为「职员职务；实习期」，多用于法律与医疗领域
由拉丁词根 cleric 构成，义为「文书的；办公室工作的」

senses.title: A worker serving customers in a shop
senses.definition: a person whose job is to serve customers in a store
senses.definitionCN: 在商店里为顾客服务的人
senses.example: The clerk helped me find the right size of shoes.
senses.exampleCN: 店员帮我找到了合适尺码的鞋子。
senses.why: Shops need someone standing behind the counter to hand goods over, so the person doing that job got this name.
senses.whyCN: 商店需要有人站在柜台后递出商品，做这份工作的人便得到了这个称呼。

senses.title: An office worker keeping records
senses.definition: a person who keeps records and accounts in an office
senses.definitionCN: 在办公室里保管记录和账目的人
senses.example: The clerk filed all the letters in the big cabinet.
senses.exampleCN: 职员把所有信件都归档进大柜子里。
senses.why: Offices run on papers and lists, and the worker who handles them daily became known as the clerk.
senses.whyCN: 办公室靠文件和清单运转，每天处理这些文件的工人就成了 clerk。

senses.title: An official who keeps records for a court or town
senses.definition: an official who keeps records for a court, a town or a club
senses.definitionCN: 为法庭、城镇或社团保管记录的公务人员
senses.example: The court clerk read out the case number.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭书记员念出了案件编号。
senses.why: Because record-keeping was once done by church-trained men, the official sense grew out of the clerical one.
senses.whyCN: 因为记录工作最早由教会培养的人来做，这个公务义项便从教士义延伸出来。

intro.en: Clerk and cleric are twins: the word began as a title for churchmen.
intro.cn: clerk 与 cleric 是双胞胎：这个词最初是教士的头衔。

items.en: Greek kleros meant a lot or share of land, later the clergy as God's share.
items.cn: 希腊语 kleros 本指抽签分得的份地，后来指「属于上帝的一份」即教士。

items.en: Late Latin clericus meant a clergyman, a man who could read and write.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 clericus 指教士，即识字、能读写的人。

items.en: Old English cleric borrowed the word for churchmen, the few people who kept records.
items.cn: 古英语借入 cleric 一词称呼教士——当时少数会做记录的人。

items.en: Old French clerc passed the word on with both the church sense and the writer sense.
items.cn: 古法语 clerc 把「教士」和「写字人」两层意思一并传了过来。

items.en: Middle English clerk slowly shifted from holy men to paid record-keepers and shop workers.
items.cn: 中古英语 clerk 渐渐从神职人员转指拿工资的记录员和店员。

items.en: Modern English kept the spelling but split the sound: British /klɑːk/, American /klɜːrk/.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了拼写但读音分了家：英式 /klɑːk/，美式 /klɜːrk/。

note.en: The first group collects words that look or sound close to clerk; the second collects people who work in offices and shops.
note.cn: 第一组收与 clerk 拼写或读音相近的词，第二组收在办公室和商店工作的人员。

entries.definition: The priests and religious workers of a religion as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「神职人员」，与 clerk 同源于拉丁语 clericus。

entries.definition: A priest or religious leader.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「教士；神职人员」，是 clerk 的拉丁同族词。

entries.definition: Quick at learning or doing things.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「聪明的」，拼写开头与 clerk 相近但词源无关。

entries.definition: A person who takes money in a shop or bank.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「收银员；出纳员」，与店员工作相近。

entries.definition: A person who handles letters and records in an office.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「秘书」，与办公室文书职责相近。

entries.definition: A person who helps a customer or a boss in a shop or office.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「助手；店员」，口语中店员常叫 sales assistant。

normalIntro.en: Remember clerk through its church past and its office present.
normalIntro.cn: 从教士出身与办公室现在两个角度记忆 clerk。

normal.en: clerk and cleric come from the same Latin word.
normal.cn: clerk 与 cleric 来自同一个拉丁词。

normal.en: British people say /klɑːk/ with no r sound.
normal.cn: 英国人读 /klɑːk/，几乎听不到 r 音。

normal.en: A desk clerk sits at the hotel front desk.
normal.cn: desk clerk 坐在酒店前台。

normal.en: A bank clerk counts money and files papers.
normal.cn: bank clerk 数钱、整理单据。

normal.en: clerical work means office paperwork jobs.
normal.cn: clerical work 指办公室文书工作。

abstract.en: Picture a man behind the counter handing shoes over the glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人在柜台后隔着玻璃递出鞋子。

abstract.en: Hear the quiet tick of a pen as records are written.
abstract.cn: 听记录落笔时笔尖安静的沙沙声。

abstract.en: Feel the stack of papers that only one person knows how to file.
abstract.cn: 感受那一摞只有一个人知道怎么归档的文件。

examples.en: The clerk wrapped the gift and wished me a happy birthday.
examples.cn: 店员包好礼物，祝我生日快乐。

examples.en: My aunt works as a clerk in the city office.
examples.cn: 我阿姨在市政办公室当职员。

examples.en: Ask the shop clerk before you change the shoes.
examples.cn: 换鞋之前先问问店员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克拉可」——克拉钻太贵，柜台职员可怜地擦了又擦，clerk 是柜台后的那个人。

root: 希腊语 kleros（份地）→ 晚期拉丁语 clericus（教士）→ 古英语 cleric、古法语 clerc → 中古英语 clerk（记录员）→ 现代英语 clerk；同族词有 clergy（神职人员）、cleric（教士）、clerical（文书的）。

sensesIntro.en: Clerk moved from church writers to office workers and then to shop helpers.
sensesIntro.cn: clerk 从教会的写字人延伸到办公室职员，再到商店店员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the person behind the desk who keeps things in order
core.cn: 核心意象：桌后那个把一切整理得井井有条的人

intro.en: Clerk built a small family around reading, writing and church life.
intro.cn: clerk 围绕读写与教会生活形成了一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root cleric means a reader of the church.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 cleric 意为教会里的读书人。

items.meaning: the priests of a religion as a whole
items.example: The clergy gathered in the old church.
items.exampleCN: 神职人员在老教堂聚会。

items.example: A senior cleric gave the speech.
items.exampleCN: 一位资深教士发表了讲话。

items.example: She does clerical work for the school.

items.meaning: a period of working as a clerk
items.example: He finished his law clerkship last year.
items.exampleCN: 他去年完成了法律实习。

items.meaning: a person handling letters for a boss
items.example: The secretary booked the meeting room.
The cashier gave me the receipt.
The typist finished the report quickly.
items.exampleCN: 打字员很快完成了报告。

items.meaning: a person greeting visitors at a desk
items.example: The receptionist smiled at the guests.
items.exampleCN: 前台接待员对客人微笑。

definition_zh: 聪明的；机灵的；灵巧的；巧妙的
definition_en: quick at learning and understanding; skillful with hands or ideas
core_image: 脑子转得飞快的孩子，眨眨眼就想出了好主意
scene: 数学课上，弟弟用巧妙的办法秒答了难题。My little brother found a clever way to solve the problem.
sceneCN: 这里 clever 是「巧妙的」（第 3 个义项：办法设计得聪明又灵巧）；句意是弟弟用巧妙的方法解出了难题。

derivatives.zh: 由 clever  + suffix  -ly 构成，义为「聪明地；巧妙地」
由 clever  + suffix  -ness 构成，义为「聪明；机灵」

senses.title: Quick at learning and understanding
senses.definition: able to learn and understand things quickly
senses.definitionCN: 能很快学会和理解事物
senses.example: She is a clever girl who reads a book every week.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个聪明的女孩，每周读一本书。
senses.why: A fast mind grabs new ideas quickly, so quick learners are called clever.
senses.whyCN: 脑子快的人能迅速抓住新想法，于是学得快的人被称作 clever。

senses.title: Skillful with the hands
senses.definition: good at making or doing things with your hands
senses.definitionCN: 擅长用手制作或操作
senses.example: Grandma is clever with her hands and knits warm scarves.
senses.exampleCN: 奶奶手很巧，会织暖和的围巾。
senses.why: The word first described handy fingers, and this older sense still survives.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早形容灵巧的手指，这一较早的义项沿用至今。

senses.title: Smart in a way that shows quick thinking
senses.definition: showing skill in thinking of a good idea or plan
senses.definitionCN: 在想法或计划上显出聪明劲
senses.example: That was a clever answer in the quiz game.
senses.exampleCN: 在问答游戏里那个回答很巧妙。
senses.why: A plan that saves time and effort feels like the work of a quick mind.
senses.whyCN: 省时省力的计划让人想到敏捷的头脑。

intro.en: Clever is a young word with a shadowy past: nobody knows exactly where it was born.
intro.cn: clever 是个年轻的词，出身成谜：没人确切知道它诞生于何处。

items.en: The origin is uncertain. Many scholars think it began as a dialect word meaning handy with tools.
items.cn: 来源不确定。许多学者认为它最初是个方言词，意为摆弄工具很在行。

items.en: Middle English had related forms such as cliver in eastern dialects, but the line to clever is not clear.
items.cn: 中古英语东部方言里有 cliver 等相关形式，但与 clever 的传承关系并不清楚。

items.en: Clever is first recorded in the late sixteenth century, meaning skillful with the hands.
items.cn: clever 最早记录于十六世纪晚期，本义是手巧。

items.en: During the seventeenth century the sense widened from handy fingers to a quick mind.
items.cn: 十七世纪间词义从灵巧的手指扩展到敏捷的头脑。

items.en: Modern English also uses clever for neat tricks and sometimes jokes about being too clever.
items.cn: 现代英语还用 clever 形容巧妙的点子，有时也用 too clever by half 调侃自作聪明的人。

note.en: The first group collects look-alike words; the second collects words about being smart.
note.cn: 第一组收形近词，第二组收表示聪明的词。

entries.definition: In a smart or skillful way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「聪明地；巧妙地」，是 clever 加 -ly 构成的派生词。

entries.definition: The quality of being clever.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「聪明；机灵」，是 clever 加 -ness 构成的派生词。

entries.definition: A bar used for lifting things.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「杠杆」，拼写与 clever 接近但词源不同。

entries.definition: Clever and quick-thinking, often in a practical way.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「机敏的」，美式口语更常用。

entries.definition: Clever, often said of children.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「伶俐的」，常形容孩子。

entries.definition: Clever through experience and good judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「智慧的」，强调经验与判断力。

normalIntro.en: Remember clever through its hand skill and its family words.
normalIntro.cn: 通过「手巧」本义与派生词记忆 clever。

normal.en: clever first meant handy with your hands.
normal.cn: clever 最初指手巧。

normal.en: cleverly is clever plus the adverb ending -ly.
normal.cn: cleverly 是 clever  + 副词 suffix  -ly。

normal.en: cleverness turns the adjective into a noun.
normal.cn: cleverness 把形容词变成名词。

normal.en: clever at maths means good at maths.
normal.cn: clever at maths 指擅长数学。

normal.en: smart and bright are common near words.
normal.cn: smart 和 bright 是常见近义词。

abstract.en: See a child lift one eyebrow and the answer appears.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子挑了挑眉，答案就冒了出来。

abstract.en: Feel fingers folding paper quickly into a perfect crane.
abstract.cn: 感受手指飞快折出完美纸鹤。

abstract.en: Watch a chess move flash like a light bulb.
abstract.cn: 想象一步棋像灯泡一样闪亮。

examples.en: The clever fox got the cheese from the crow.
examples.cn: 机灵的狐狸从乌鸦那里骗到了奶酪。

examples.en: She is clever at maths and never fears the exam.
examples.cn: 她擅长数学，从不害怕考试。

examples.en: His clever plan saved us a whole afternoon.
examples.cn: 他巧妙的计划为我们省了一下午。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克莱沃」——克莱沃每次考试都「快而沃」（快而多），因为他很聪明。

root: 来源不确定；一般认为源自东部方言中表示「手巧」的词，与中古英语 cliver 等形式关系存疑 → 十六世纪晚期首见 → 现代英语 clever；派生词有 cleverly（巧妙地）、cleverness（聪明）。

sensesIntro.en: Clever grew from handy fingers to a quick mind and clever ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: clever 从灵巧的双手延伸到敏捷的头脑和巧妙的点子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mind or a pair of hands that works fast and well
core.cn: 核心意象：一双转得快、做得好的手或头脑

intro.en: Clever keeps its family small: an adverb, a noun and its near words.
intro.cn: clever 词族不大：一个副词、一个名词，再加几个近义词。

latinIntro.en: Clever is not Latin; it is an English dialect word with an unclear past.
latinIntro.cn: clever 不是拉丁词，而是出身不明的英语方言词。

items.example: She cleverly fixed the broken kite.
items.exampleCN: 她巧妙地修好了坏掉的风筝。

items.example: Everyone admired the boy's cleverness.
items.exampleCN: 大家都很佩服那男孩的机灵。

items.example: That is a smart choice.
She is a bright little girl.
The old owl looks very wise.
items.exampleCN: 老猫头鹰看起来很有智慧。

items.meaning: a person with very great ability
items.example: Einstein is called a genius.
The skillful cook cut the fruit fast.
items.exampleCN: 熟练的厨师切水果很快。

items.example: His quick-witted reply made us laugh.
items.exampleCN: 他机敏的回答逗笑了我们。

definition_zh: 咔哒声；（鼠标）点击；发出咔哒声；一下子合拍
definition_en: a short sharp sound; to press a mouse button; to get on well suddenly
core_image: 开关按下的那一声轻脆的「咔哒」
scene: 夜里，弟弟轻轻关上台灯，只听一声轻响。The lamp made a soft click in the dark room.
sceneCN: 这里 click 是「咔哒声」（第 1 个义项：短促清脆的声音）；句意是台灯在黑暗的房间里发出轻脆的咔哒声。

collocations.zh: 咔哒一声就位；豁然开朗

derivatives.zh: 由 click 加 bait 构成，义为「标题党；诱饵标题」，指吸引点击的标题
由 click  + suffix  -er 构成，义为「遥控器；翻页器」

senses.title: A short sharp sound
senses.definition: a short, light, sharp sound
senses.definitionCN: 一声短促轻脆的声音
senses.example: The door locked with a click.
senses.exampleCN: 门咔哒一声锁上了。
senses.why: Small metal parts knock together and give out this sharp little sound, so the sound got its own name.
senses.whyCN: 金属小部件相碰会发出这种脆响，这声音便有了名字。

senses.title: To press a mouse button
senses.definition: to press one of the buttons on a computer mouse
senses.definitionCN: 按下鼠标上的按键
senses.example: Click the picture to hear the song.
senses.exampleCN: 点击这张图片就能听到这首歌。
senses.why: The mouse button makes the same little sound, so the action borrowed the noise for a name.
senses.whyCN: 鼠标按键按下时发出同样的小响声，这个动作便借用了响声的名字。

senses.title: To suddenly understand or get on well
senses.definition: to become clear or friendly very suddenly
senses.definitionCN: 突然变得清楚或融洽
senses.example: At last the maths question clicked for me.
senses.exampleCN: 我终于一下子弄懂了那道数学题。
senses.why: When parts fit, they snap together with a click; minds and friendships can snap together the same way.
senses.whyCN: 部件合适时会咔哒一声咬合，思路和友谊也会这样一下子咬合。

intro.en: Click is a word copied from sound itself: someone heard it and wrote it down.
intro.cn: click 是从声音本身抄下来的词：有人听到了，便把它写了下来。

items.en: Click is imitative: it copies the sharp sound it names, so its roots do not lead back to Latin or Greek.
items.cn: click 是拟声词：它模仿自己所指的脆响，因此词根并不追溯到拉丁语或希腊语。

items.en: The noun click for a sharp sound is first recorded in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 表示脆响的名词 click 最早记录于十七世纪。

items.en: The verb soon followed, for things that make that sound or lock together.
items.cn: 动词随后出现，指发出这种声音或咬合的动作。

items.en: In the twentieth century the computer mouse borrowed the word for pressing its button.
items.cn: 二十世纪，计算机鼠标借用了这个词来表示按键动作。

items.en: Later still, people said something clicks when an idea or a friendship suddenly fits.
items.cn: 更晚人们用 something clicks 表示想法或友谊一下子契合。

note.en: The first group collects sound-alike and shape-alike words; the second collects related sounds and computer actions.
note.cn: 第一组收音近形近的词，第二组收相关声音和电脑操作。

entries.definition: A machine that shows the time.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「时钟」，与 click 只差一个字母，词源无关。

entries.definition: A small device for changing slides.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「翻页器；遥控器」，由 click 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: A louder, harder knocking sound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「咔嗒声（较响）」，与 click 音近义近。

entries.definition: A light touch on a screen.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「轻点（屏幕）」，触屏时代的常用说法。

entries.definition: A sudden sharp breaking sound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「啪嗒声；断裂声」，声音更响更硬。

entries.definition: Two quick presses of a mouse button.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「双击」，由 double 加 click 构成的电脑用语。

normalIntro.en: Remember click through the sounds and screens of daily life.
normalIntro.cn: 从日常的声音与屏幕出发记忆 click。

normal.en: click copies the sound it names: click!
normal.cn: click 模仿它所指的声音：咔哒！

normal.en: click the mouse means press the mouse button.
normal.cn: click the mouse 指按鼠标键。

normal.en: click into place means things suddenly fit.
normal.cn: click into place 指事情豁然开朗。

normal.en: clock and click differ by only one letter.
normal.cn: clock 和 click 只差一个字母。

normal.en: clickbait means a title made to get clicks.
normal.cn: clickbait 指为了骗点击而起的标题。

abstract.en: Hear the tiny snap of a seat belt locking.
abstract.cn: 听安全带扣上时那声细小的脆响。

abstract.en: Feel the mouse button sink and rise under your finger.
abstract.cn: 感受鼠标键在指尖下沉又弹起。

abstract.en: Picture a puzzle piece falling into its hole.
abstract.cn: 想象一块拼图落进它该在的凹槽。

examples.en: Hear the click of the camera before the photo.
examples.cn: 拍照前能听到相机的咔哒声。

examples.en: Click the green button to send your homework.
examples.cn: 点击绿色按钮提交作业。

examples.en: The key turned with a click and the box opened.
examples.cn: 钥匙咔哒一转，盒子打开了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克利克」——鼠标一点，「克」的一声「利」落清「克」，click 就是那一声脆响。

root: 拟声词，模仿短促脆响，来源不确定 → 十七世纪首见名词 → 动词随之出现 → 现代英语扩展到鼠标点击与「一下子契合」。

sensesIntro.en: Click moves from a tiny sound to a screen action and then to minds that fit.
sensesIntro.cn: click 从一声轻响延伸到屏幕操作，再到想法的豁然开朗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two small parts meeting with one sharp sound
core.cn: 核心意象：两个小部件相碰发出一声脆响

branches.en: People getting on well at once

intro.en: Click builds simple, modern words around its tiny sound.
intro.cn: click 围绕它那声轻响造出简单而现代的词。

latinIntro.en: Click has no Latin root: it is pure imitation of sound.

items.meaning: a device that makes clicking sounds
items.example: The teacher used a clicker to change slides.
items.exampleCN: 老师用翻页器切换幻灯片。

items.meaning: a title made to attract clicks
items.example: That story was just clickbait.

items.meaning: two quick presses of the mouse
items.example: Double-click the file to open it.

items.meaning: the record of a user's clicks
items.example: The site studies its clickstream.
items.exampleCN: 网站分析自己的点击流数据。

items.example: We heard the clack of heels in the hall.
items.exampleCN: 我们听到大厅里高跟鞋的咔嗒声。

definition_zh: 爬；攀登；爬升；（植物）攀缘；（数量）上升
definition_en: to go up, especially using hands and feet; to rise slowly in amount
core_image: 手脚并用，一寸一寸把自己送上高处
scene: 周末爬山，哥哥拉着绳索一步步向上。The boys decided to climb the hill behind the school.
sceneCN: 这里 climb 是「攀登」（第 2 个义项：向上爬一座山）；句意是男孩们决定爬学校后面的那座小山。

derivatives.zh: 由 climb  + suffix  -er 构成，义为「攀登者；攀缘植物」
由 climb 加 -ing 构成，义为「登山运动；攀爬」

senses.title: To go up using hands and feet
senses.definition: to move up something using your hands and feet
senses.definitionCN: 借助手脚向上移动
senses.example: The cat likes to climb the curtains.
senses.exampleCN: 这只猫喜欢爬窗帘。
senses.why: When a surface is steep, hands join feet, and that four-limbed movement is the heart of the word.
senses.whyCN: 坡面陡峭时手和脚要一起用，这种四肢并用的动作正是词义核心。

senses.title: To go up a mountain or hill
senses.definition: to travel up a mountain or high place
senses.definitionCN: 登上山或高处
senses.example: They want to climb Mount Tai this summer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们想今年夏天去爬泰山。
senses.why: Mountains are the biggest thing anyone can go up, so the word proudly names that long hard rise.
senses.whyCN: 山是人能登上的最大之物，这个词便用来命名那段漫长艰难的攀登。

senses.title: To rise slowly in amount or level
senses.definition: to increase slowly in amount, price or level
senses.definitionCN: 数量、价格或水平缓慢增加
senses.example: The price of apples climbed again this month.
senses.exampleCN: 这个月苹果价格又涨了。
senses.why: Numbers rising on a chart look like a person going step by step up a slope.
senses.whyCN: 图表上缓缓上升的数字，就像人一步一步爬坡。

senses.title: To grow upward by holding on
senses.definition: to grow upwards by holding on to a support
senses.definitionCN: 借助支撑物向上生长
senses.example: The beans climb up the bamboo sticks.
senses.exampleCN: 豆藤顺着竹竿向上爬。
senses.why: A vine has no legs but still rises by gripping, as if it were climbing hand over hand.
senses.whyCN: 藤蔓没有脚，却靠攀附上升，仿佛在手脚并用地攀爬。

intro.en: Climb is an old walking word: English speakers have been climbing since before dictionaries existed.
intro.cn: climb 是个古老的行进词：早在词典出现之前，英语使用者就在攀爬了。

items.en: It goes back to a Germanic word *klimban, whose further origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 它来自日耳曼语 *klimban，更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Old English climban meant to mount or go up by clinging.
items.cn: 古英语 climban 意为攀附着向上爬。

items.en: Middle English climben kept the sense; German klimmen is a cousin from the same source.
items.cn: 中古英语 climben 沿用该义；德语 klimmen 是同源词。

items.en: The letter b in the spelling became silent, and now nobody hears it at all.
items.cn: 拼写中的字母 b 后来不发音，如今完全听不到。

items.en: Modern English extended climb to prices, plants and aircraft rising.
items.cn: 现代英语把 climb 扩展到价格、攀缘植物和飞机的爬升。

note.en: The first group collects the word family and spelling neighbors; the second collects words about going up.
note.cn: 第一组收词族与拼写邻居，第二组收表示上升的词。

entries.definition: A person or plant that climbs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「攀登者；攀缘植物」，是 climb 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: The sport or act of going up.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「攀登运动」，是 climb 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: An arm or a leg.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「肢体」，与 climb 拼写相近，词源无关。

entries.definition: To go up, said of numbers, sun or people.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「上升」，可用于数字、太阳或起身。

entries.definition: To go up, in a formal way.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「上升；登高」，语体较正式。

entries.definition: A simple everyday way to say move higher.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「上去」，日常口语说法。

normalIntro.en: Remember climb through its silent b and its everyday partners.
normalIntro.cn: 借助不发音的 b 与常见搭配记忆 climb。

normal.en: The b in climb is silent: say /klaɪm/.
normal.cn: climb 中的 b 不发音：读 /klaɪm/。

normal.en: climb a tree means go up a tree with hands and feet.
normal.cn: climb a tree 指手脚并用爬树。

normal.en: climber is the person who climbs.
normal.cn: climber 指攀登的人。

normal.en: Prices climb like people on stairs.
normal.cn: 价格像爬楼梯的人一样攀升。

normal.en: Vines climb up the wall in summer.
normal.cn: 夏天藤蔓沿墙向上攀缘。

abstract.en: Feel rough rock under your fingers as you rise.
abstract.cn: 想象上升时指尖下的粗糙岩石。

abstract.en: See green stems winding round a stick.
abstract.cn: 想象绿色藤蔓绕着竹竿缠绕而上。

abstract.en: Watch a small red arrow creep up the chart.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上的小红箭头慢慢爬升。

examples.en: We took an hour to climb to the top of the hill.
examples.cn: 我们花了一个小时爬到山顶。

examples.en: Prices kept climbing all winter.
examples.cn: 整个冬天价格都在攀升。

examples.en: Do not climb the fence after class.
examples.cn: 下课后不要翻越围栏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克拉伊姆」——爬墙时「裤」都磨破也不「疑」「慢」，climb 就是手脚并用往上爬。

root: 日耳曼语 *klimban（来源不确定）→ 古英语 climban（攀附而上）→ 中古英语 climben → 现代英语 climb（b 不发音）；同族词有德语 klimmen，派生词有 climber（攀登者）、climbing（登山运动）。

sensesIntro.en: Climb moves from hands-and-feet rising to mountains, prices, plants and planes.
sensesIntro.cn: climb 从手脚并用的攀爬延伸到山、价格、植物和飞机。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rising step by step against gravity
core.cn: 核心意象：一步一步对抗重力向上

intro.en: Climb keeps a small family: two -er and -ing words and its near partners.
intro.cn: climb 词族不大：两个 -er、-ing 派生词，再加几个近邻。

latinIntro.en: Climb is Germanic, not Latin, so its relatives are German words like klimmen.
latinIntro.cn: climb 属日耳曼词源而非拉丁词源，同族词是德语 klimmen 等。

items.meaning: a person or plant that climbs
items.example: The climber reached the top at noon.

items.meaning: the sport of going up rocks or mountains
items.example: Rock climbing is popular at our school.
items.exampleCN: 攀岩在我们学校很受欢迎。

items.meaning: an act of admitting you were wrong
items.example: The boss made a quiet climbdown.

items.meaning: to go up in amount or level
items.example: The sun rises in the east.
The plane ascended into the clouds.
We descended the hill slowly.

items.meaning: to go up, often with a name
items.example: They mounted the steps one by one.

items.meaningCN: 德语「爬」，与 climb 同源
items.example: German klimmen sounds like climb without the b.
items.exampleCN: 德语 klimmen 听起来像去掉 b 的 climb。

definition_zh: 诊所；门诊部；（短期的）讲习班
definition_en: a place where people receive medical treatment but do not stay overnight
core_image: 一张安静的诊疗床，医生坐在床边问诊
scene: 放学后，妈妈带弟弟去小区的门诊部看嗓子。The doctor at the clinic checked his throat quickly.
sceneCN: 这里 clinic 是「诊所；门诊部」（第 1 个义项：可以看病但不用住院的地方）；句意是诊所医生很快检查了他的喉咙。

derivatives.zh: 由 clinic  + suffix  -al 构成，义为「临床的；诊所的」
由 clinic  + suffix  -ician 构成，义为「临床医生」

senses.title: A place for medical treatment without staying overnight
senses.definition: a place where a doctor treats patients who do not stay there
senses.definitionCN: 医生为无需留宿的病人看病的地方
senses.example: The new clinic near the station opens at eight.
senses.exampleCN: 车站附近的新诊所八点开门。
senses.why: Doctors once taught at the bedside of patients, and the place where this happened became the clinic.
senses.whyCN: 医生早先在病人床边教学查房，这一地点便得名 clinic。

senses.title: A special medical service or course
senses.titleCN: 专科门诊；（学校的）健康服务
senses.definition: an organized medical service for one special problem
senses.definitionCN: 针对某一专门问题的医疗服务
senses.example: The school runs an eye clinic every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 学校每年春天开设眼科门诊。
senses.why: One problem, one room, one team: medicine splits big care into focused little units.
senses.whyCN: 一个问题、一间诊室、一组医生：医疗把大病区拆成聚焦的小单元。

senses.title: A short course of practical teaching
senses.definition: a short class where a skill is taught in practice
senses.definitionCN: 短期传授某项技能的实践课
senses.example: Uncle Wang teaches at a free basketball clinic on Sundays.
senses.exampleCN: 王叔叔周日在免费篮球训练营教球。
senses.why: Doctors' bedside lessons felt like coaching, so other sports borrowed the word for skill classes.
senses.whyCN: 医生的床边教学像示范训练，其他项目便借用这个词指技能班。

intro.en: Clinic begins with a bed: the whole word family grows from lying down.
intro.cn: clinic 始于一张床：整个词族都从「躺卧」生长出来。

items.en: Greek kline meant a bed or couch on which sick people lay.
items.cn: 希腊语 kline 指病人躺卧的床或长榻。

items.en: Latin clinicus described a doctor who visited patients at their beds.
items.cn: 拉丁语 clinicus 描述到病床边诊视的医生。

items.en: French clinique kept the bedside sense for medical teaching hospitals.
items.cn: 法语 clinique 保留了「床边教学医院」的含义。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the eighteenth century for bedside medical teaching.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入该词，指床边医学教学。

items.en: Later English used clinic for the building and then for short practical courses.
items.cn: 后来 clinic 又指诊所建筑，再引申为短期讲习班。

note.en: The first group collects the clinic word family; the second collects places that give care.
note.cn: 第一组收 clinic 词族，第二组收提供医疗照护的场所。

entries.definition: Relating to the treatment of patients.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「临床的」，由 clinic 加 -al 构成。

entries.definition: A doctor who works directly with patients.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「临床医生」，由 clinic 加 -ician 构成。

entries.definition: To hold on tightly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「紧抓」，拼写与 clinic 开头相近，词源无关。

entries.definition: A large place for serious illness and overnight care.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「医院」，规模更大、可住院。

entries.definition: In British English, a doctor's office.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，英式英语义为「医生的诊室」。

entries.definition: A small room for sick students or workers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「医务室」，常在学校或工厂。

normalIntro.en: Remember clinic through its bed root and its family words.
normalIntro.cn: 通过「床」的词根与词族记忆 clinic。

normal.en: clinic comes from a Greek word for bed.
normal.cn: clinic 来自希腊语「床」。

normal.en: clinical means connected with treating patients.
normal.cn: clinical 意为「临床的」。

normal.en: clinician is the doctor in a clinic.
normal.cn: clinician 指诊所里的临床医生。

normal.en: A dental clinic cares for teeth.
normal.cn: dental clinic 看牙。

normal.en: Sports teams hold clinics to teach skills.
normal.cn: 运动队用 clinic 开设技能班。

abstract.en: Picture a doctor pulling a chair beside a bed.
abstract.cn: 想象医生把椅子拉到床边坐下。

abstract.en: Hear the low murmur of questions and answers at the bedside.
abstract.cn: 听床边一问一答的低语。

abstract.en: Feel the calm order of a small, tidy consulting room.
abstract.cn: 感受小诊室里安静有序的气氛。

examples.en: Grandma goes to the clinic for her blood test every month.
examples.cn: 奶奶每个月去诊所验血。

examples.en: The sports clinic taught me how to pass the ball.
examples.cn: 训练营教会了我怎么传球。

examples.en: The clinic was quiet because the doctor was out on a call.
examples.cn: 诊所很安静，因为医生出诊去了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克里尼克」——病人躺在「床」上，医生克勤克俭地护理，clinic 就是床边的小诊所。

root: 希腊语 kline（床）→ 拉丁语 clinicus（到床边诊视的医生）→ 法语 clinique → 十八世纪英语 clinic（床边教学）→ 现代英语「诊所」；派生词有 clinical（临床的）、clinician（临床医生）。

sensesIntro.en: Clinic grew from a bedside lesson to a treatment room and a training class.
sensesIntro.cn: clinic 从床边教学延伸到诊疗室，再到技能训练班。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the doctor's chair beside the patient's bed
core.cn: 核心意象：病床边医生的那把椅子

intro.en: The bed root builds a whole medical family.
intro.cn: 「床」词根繁衍出整个医疗词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin and Greek roots kline and clinare both come from the same idea of leaning and lying.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 kline 与拉丁语 clinare 都出自「倚靠、躺卧」这同一个意象。

items.example: She watched the clinical practice video.
A good clinician listens first.
Greek kline lies inside the word clinic.
items.exampleCN: clinic 一词里藏着希腊语 kline。

items.structure: Latin root clin  with prefix in-
items.example: I incline towards the second plan.

items.structure: Latin root clin  with prefix de-
items.example: Sales began to decline in May.

items.structure: Latin root clin  with prefix re-
items.example: The seat reclines for a rest.
The hospital has many departments.
The polyclinic sees both eyes and teeth.
items.exampleCN: 综合门诊部既看眼也看牙。

latinEntries.meaning: a doctor who treats patients at the bedside
to visit and examine the sick

definition_zh: 钟；时钟；（生理）生物钟
definition_en: an instrument that shows the time, usually standing or hanging free
core_image: 挂在墙上的圆钟，秒针一格一格地走
scene: 教室后面挂着一只圆钟，秒针沙沙地走。The clock on the wall shows three twenty.
sceneCN: 这里 clock 是「时钟」（第 1 个义项：报时的仪器）；句意是墙上的钟显示三点二十分。

derivatives.zh: 由 clock 加 wise 构成，义为「顺时针方向的」
由 clock 加 work 构成，义为「钟表装置；发条机构」

senses.title: An instrument that shows the time
senses.definition: an instrument that shows the time and is not worn on the body
senses.definitionCN: 报时的仪器，不随身佩戴
senses.example: The old clock struck twelve at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 老钟在午夜敲了十二下。
senses.why: Watches sit on the wrist, but bigger timekeepers stand or hang, and those got the name clock.
senses.whyCN: 手表戴在手腕，更大的报时器立着或挂着，这些被称为 clock。

senses.title: An inner sense of time
senses.definition: an inner sense or rhythm that measures time inside a living thing
senses.definitionCN: 生物体内感知时间的内在节律
senses.example: My body clock wakes me before the alarm.
senses.exampleCN: 我的生物钟在闹钟响之前叫醒了我。
senses.why: People measure time as steadily as a machine, so the machine's name was borrowed for the inner rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 人对时间的感知像机器一样规律，于是机器的名字被借来指内在节律。

senses.title: The odometer of a car
senses.definition: the meter showing how far a car has travelled
senses.definitionCN: 显示汽车行驶里程的仪表
senses.example: The car has 100000 kilometres on the clock.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆车里程表上已有十万公里。
senses.why: Both a clock and an odometer count steadily onwards, so the counting face shares the name.
senses.whyCN: 钟和里程表都在稳定地计数，计数表盘便共享了这个名字。

intro.en: Clock is a bell word: the earliest clocks did not have faces, they just rang.
intro.cn: clock 本是「铃」：最早的钟没有表盘，只会响。

items.en: The old Germanic base klokka imitated the round sound of a bell.
items.cn: 古老的日耳曼词基 klokka 模仿铃铛圆润的响声。

items.en: Old Norse klokka carried the bell-word north.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 klokka 把这个「铃」词带到北方。

items.en: Old French cloque meant a bell and, later, the ringing of a bell.
items.cn: 古法语 cloque 既指铃，也指铃声。

items.en: Middle English took clock from the French; then the word moved from bell to timepiece.
items.cn: 中古英语从法语借来 clock；词义随后从铃转到计时器。

items.en: Modern English kept clock for the timekeeper and built around the clock for endless work.
items.cn: 现代英语以 clock 指计时器，又造出 around the clock 表示昼夜不停。

note.en: The first group collects look-alike words; the second collects time words and devices.
note.cn: 第一组收形近词，第二组收时间相关词与装置。

entries.definition: A short sharp sound or a mouse action.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「咔哒声；点击」，与 clock 仅一个字母之差。

entries.definition: Moving in the direction of clock hands.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「顺时针」，由 clock 加 wise 构成。

entries.definition: A solid piece or to stop.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「街区；堵塞」，与 clock 拼写相近但词源无关。

entries.definition: A small clock worn on the wrist.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「手表」，戴在手腕上。

entries.definition: A device that counts down a set time.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「计时器」，倒计时用。

entries.definition: An old device that times by falling sand.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「沙漏」，古老的计时工具。

normalIntro.en: Remember clock through its bell past and its daily partners.
normalIntro.cn: 通过「铃」的过去与日常搭配记忆 clock。

normal.en: clock began as a bell-word: cloque in French.
normal.cn: clock 起先是「铃」，法语作 cloque。

normal.en: an alarm clock wakes you up.
normal.cn: alarm clock 是闹钟。

normal.en: around the clock means all day and all night.
normal.cn: around the clock 指昼夜不停。

normal.en: clockwise follows the hands of a clock.
normal.cn: clockwise 顺时针。

normal.en: clock in means record your work time.
normal.cn: clock in 指打卡上班。

abstract.en: Hear twelve slow strikes from a tall tower at midnight.
abstract.cn: 想象午夜塔楼传来十二下钟声。

abstract.en: See red numbers glowing softly in a dark bedroom.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗卧室里柔和发亮的红色数字。

abstract.en: Feel the seconds tick under your skin like a hidden spring.
abstract.cn: 感受秒针像藏在体内的发条一样跳动。

examples.en: The clock stopped, so we were late for class.
examples.cn: 钟停了，所以我们上课迟到了。

examples.en: Repair crews worked around the clock after the storm.
examples.cn: 风暴过后抢修队昼夜不停地工作。

examples.en: Grandpa winds the old clock every Sunday morning.
examples.cn: 爷爷每周日早晨给老钟上发条。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克罗克」——钟「克」是圆的，钟「壳」挂墙上，「克罗克」就是那只报时的钟。

root: 日耳曼语 klokka（拟声「铃」）→ 古诺斯语 klokka → 古法语 cloque（铃；铃声）→ 中古英语 clok → 现代英语 clock；派生词有 clockwise（顺时针）、clockwork（发条装置）。

sensesIntro.en: Clock grew from a bell to a timepiece and then to rhythms and meters.
sensesIntro.cn: clock 从「铃」变成计时器，再延伸到生物节律与里程表。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steady circle that never stops counting
core.cn: 核心意象：一个永不停歇、稳定计数的圆

intro.en: Clock builds a tidy family of time machines.
intro.cn: clock 繁衍出一家干净的计时装置词族。

latinIntro.en: Clock is Germanic, so its Latin connection is only through later compounds.
latinIntro.cn: clock 属日耳曼词源，与拉丁语的关联只体现在后来的复合词上。

items.meaning: in the direction of clock hands
items.example: Turn the knob clockwise.
Stir the soup anticlockwise.
The toy runs on clockwork.
Set the alarm clock for six.

items.meaning: a small clock worn on the wrist
items.example: The watch has a leather band.
The timer beeped at ten minutes.

items.meaning: a swinging weight in old clocks
items.example: The pendulum swings left and right.
Turn the hourglass over.

definition_zh: 关；关闭；结束；（在）附近的；亲密的
definition_en: to shut something; near in distance or feeling; to come to an end
core_image: 把门轻轻带上，或者把心靠得更近
scene: 晚自习结束，值日生把教室的门关上。Please close the door when you leave the classroom.
sceneCN: 这里 close 是「关上」（第 1 个义项：使门窗合上）；句意是离开教室时请随手关门。

derivatives.zh: 由 close  + suffix  -ly 构成，义为「紧密地；仔细地」
由 close  + suffix  -ness 构成，义为「接近；亲密」
由拉丁词根 clud 构成，义为「关闭；停业」

senses.title: To shut something
senses.definition: to move a door, lid or window so that it is shut
senses.definitionCN: 使门、盖子或窗户合上
senses.example: Close your book and look at me.
senses.exampleCN: 合上书，看着我。
senses.why: Two parts of a thing are pushed together until nothing shows, and that meeting is the shut state.
senses.whyCN: 把物体的两部分推拢直到不再露缝，相合即是关闭。

senses.title: To end an event, shop or work
senses.definition: to stop an activity, a business or a meeting
senses.definitionCN: 让活动、商店或会议停止
senses.example: The shop closes at nine every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店每晚九点关门。
senses.why: When the day's doors shut, work is done: shutting the door ends the day.
senses.whyCN: 当一天的门被关上，工作便告完成：关门即结束。

senses.title: Near in distance
senses.definition: only a short distance away
senses.definitionCN: 距离很短
senses.example: Our school is close to the bus station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们学校离汽车站很近。
senses.why: Shut things sit tight against each other, so touching things are called close.
senses.whyCN: 合拢的东西紧贴在一起，紧贴之物便叫「近」。

senses.title: Near in feeling
senses.definition: knowing and liking someone very well
senses.definitionCN: 彼此非常了解、喜欢
senses.example: She is my closest friend in the class.
senses.exampleCN: 她是我在班里最亲密的朋友。
senses.why: Hearts can shut out the world and keep only one person inside, like a small closed circle.
senses.whyCN: 心可以把世界关在门外，只留一人于内，如一个小小的闭合圆圈。

senses.title: Narrow in result
senses.definition: nearly equal in a game or competition
senses.definitionCN: 比赛或竞争中几乎不相上下
senses.example: It was a close match, but we won by two points.
senses.exampleCN: 比分很胶着，我们以两分险胜。
senses.why: A tight contest keeps the two sides closed together till the end.
senses.whyCN: 激烈的比赛让双方一直咬得很紧。

intro.en: Close carries two doors in one word: a Latin verb for shutting, and Old French to carry it in.
intro.cn: close 一词里有两扇门：拉丁语的「关」动词，以及把它送来的古法语。

items.en: Latin claudere meant to shut, withcludere in compounds like conclude and include.
items.cn: 拉丁语 claudere 意为关闭，复合词如 conclude、include 中的 -cludere 同根。

items.en: Old French clos and clore passed on the sense of shutting and enclosing.
items.cn: 古法语 clos 与 clore 传下了关闭、围拢之义。

items.en: Middle English closen first meant to shut doors and fences.
items.cn: 中古英语 closen 最初指关上门和栅栏。

items.en: The verb settled as /kləʊz/ while the adjective stayed /kləʊs/.
items.cn: 动词读音定为 /kləʊz/，形容词保持 /kləʊs/。

items.en: Modern English widened close from doors to feelings, prices and endings.
items.cn: 现代英语把 close 从门扩展到情感、价格与结局。

note.en: The first group collects the Latin clud family; the second collects words for shutting and being near.
note.cn: 第一组收拉丁语 clud 词族，第二组收表示关闭与接近的词。

entries.definition: A small room or cupboard for clothes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「壁橱」，与 close 同源于拉丁语 claudere。

entries.definition: The act of closing a road, school or business.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「关闭；停业」，与 close 同根。

entries.definition: Things you wear.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「衣服」，与 close 拼写相近但词源不同。

entries.definition: To close something, an everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「关上」，日常用词。

entries.definition: A short distance away.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「近的」，与 close 第 3 义项同义。

entries.definition: To end a meeting or a speech.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「结束；得出结论」，与 close 同源。

normalIntro.en: Remember close through its shut verb and its near adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 从动词「关」与形容词「近」两侧记忆 close。

normal.en: As a verb, close ends with a /z/ sound.
normal.cn: 作动词时 close 结尾发 /z/。

normal.en: As an adjective, close ends with an /s/ sound.
normal.cn: 作形容词时 close 结尾发 /s/。

normal.en: close friends are people you trust most.
normal.cn: close friends 指最信任的朋友。

normal.en: close down means a shop stops business.
normal.cn: close down 指商店停业。

normal.en: conclude and include share the same root clud.
normal.cn: conclude 和 include 同含词根 clud。

abstract.en: Hear the soft thud of a door pulled gently shut.
abstract.cn: 听轻轻合上门的那声闷响。

abstract.en: Feel two hands pressed palm to palm, nothing between.
abstract.cn: 感受两手掌心相贴、中间无缝。

abstract.en: See a race photo where two runners cross together.
abstract.cn: 想象两张冲线的照片里，两名选手几乎并排。

examples.en: Close the window, please, it is cold outside.
examples.cn: 请关上窗户，外面很冷。

examples.en: The library closes at eight in the evening.
examples.cn: 图书馆晚上八点闭馆。

examples.en: We lost a close game by only one goal.
examples.cn: 我们只差一球输掉了这场势均力敌的比赛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克罗斯」——门一「克罗斯」就关紧了，克罗斯的家「靠近」教室，关系「亲密」。

root: 拉丁语 claudere（关闭）→ 古法语 clos/clore → 中古英语 closen → 现代英语 close；同族词有 conclude（结束）、include（包含）、closet（壁橱）、closure（关闭）。

sensesIntro.en: Close moves from shutting doors to ending events, to near places and near hearts.
sensesIntro.cn: close 从关门延伸到结束活动，再到距离之近与心灵之亲。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two parts meeting until nothing is left between
core.cn: 核心意象：两部分相合，中间不留缝隙

intro.en: The Latin root clud builds a big family of shut and meet words.
intro.cn: 拉丁词根 clud 繁衍出庞大的「关」与「合」词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin claudere, to shut, hides inside conclude, include and exclude.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 claudere（关闭）藏在 conclude、include、exclude 之中。

items.example: She hung her coat in the closet.
The bridge closure lasted a month.
items.exampleCN: 大桥关闭持续了一个月。

items.example: The meeting concluded at five.
The price includes breakfast.
They excluded late entries.
items.exampleCN: 他们排除了迟交的报名。

items.example: The writer secluded himself in a village.
items.exampleCN: 作家把自己隔绝在村中。

items.example: He kept a closeted dream of music.
Shut the gate behind you.

definition_zh: 布；布料；一块布
definition_en: material made by weaving cotton, wool or other fibres
core_image: 一匹柔软的布，指尖一摸便起细纹
scene: 美术课上，同学们用一块布擦掉颜料。Wipe the paint with a soft cloth, please.
sceneCN: 这里 cloth 是「一块布」（第 2 个义项：用来擦东西的那块布料）；句意是请用软布擦掉颜料。

derivatives.zh: 由 cloth  + suffix  -e 构成，义为「给…穿衣」
由 cloth 派生，义为「衣服」的总称
由 cloth 加 -ing 构成，义为「服装（总称）」

senses.title: Woven material
senses.definition: material made of woven fibres like cotton or wool
senses.definitionCN: 棉、毛等纤维织成的材料
senses.example: Mother bought two metres of cloth to make curtains.
senses.exampleCN: 妈妈买了两米布做窗帘。
senses.why: Weaving turns loose fibres into a flat sheet, and the flat sheet itself got the name.
senses.whyCN: 织造把松散纤维变成平整的一幅，这一整幅便得了名字。

senses.title: A piece of this material for cleaning
senses.definition: a single piece of cloth used to clean or cover things
senses.definitionCN: 用来擦东西或盖东西的一块布
senses.example: Hand me a damp cloth to wipe the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 递给我一块湿布擦桌子。
senses.why: A big sheet can be torn into small handy pieces for wiping, so a wipe-rag keeps the same name.
senses.whyCN: 大布可以撕成小块随手擦用，擦布便沿用同一名字。

senses.title: The textile trade or making
senses.definition: the making and selling of woven material
senses.definitionCN: 布料的织造与买卖
senses.example: The town lived on cloth for two hundred years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小城靠纺织活了二百年。
senses.why: When one material feeds a whole town, the material's name covers the trade too.
senses.whyCN: 当一种物料养活全城，它的名字也覆盖了这门行业。

intro.en: Cloth is one of the oldest words of everyday life, older than any written story about tailors.
intro.cn: cloth 是日常生活最古老的词之一，比任何关于裁缝的记载都古老。

items.en: The Germanic base *klotham is the starting point; its earlier origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 起点是日耳曼语词基 *klotham，更早来源不确定。

items.en: Old English clath meant a cloth or a garment.
items.cn: 古英语 clath 指布或衣物。

items.en: German Tuch and Dutch doek are cousins from the same old family.
items.cn: 德语 Tuch 与荷兰语 doek 是同一古老家族的亲戚。

items.en: Middle English cloth covered both the material and the made garment.
items.cn: 中古英语 cloth 既指材料也指做成的衣服。

items.en: Modern English split the work: cloth for material, clothes for worn things, clothing for the whole trade.
items.cn: 现代英语分工明确：cloth 指布料，clothes 指穿的衣服，clothing 指服装总称。

note.en: The first group collects the cloth family; the second collects fabric words.
note.cn: 第一组收 cloth 词族，第二组收面料类词。

entries.definition: Things you wear.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「衣服」，与 cloth 同源却只指成衣。

entries.definition: Garments in general.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「服装（总称）」，由 cloth 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: A maker or seller of clothes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「服装商；裁缝」，是 cloth 的老派生词。

entries.definition: Material made by weaving, often fine cloth.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「织物；面料」，与 cloth 同义而稍正式。

entries.definition: The stuff things are made from.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「材料」，范围更广。

entries.definition: Woven cloth, often in trade contexts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「纺织品」，多用于行业语境。

normalIntro.en: Remember cloth through its three relatives: clothe, clothes and clothing.
normalIntro.cn: 借三个亲戚 clothe、clothes、clothing 记忆 cloth。

normal.en: cloth is the material; clothes are what you wear.
normal.cn: cloth 是布料，clothes 是穿的衣服。

normal.en: the plural of cloth is cloths.
normal.cn: cloth 的复数是 cloths。

normal.en: a damp cloth wipes tables clean.
normal.cn: 湿布能把桌子擦干净。

normal.en: clothe the baby means put clothes on the baby.
normal.cn: clothe the baby 指给宝宝穿衣。

normal.en: cotton cloth feels soft in summer.
normal.cn: 棉布夏天摸起来柔软。

abstract.en: Feel the cool smooth slide of silk between your fingers.
abstract.cn: 感受丝缎在指间清凉顺滑地滑过。

abstract.en: Hear the soft swish of cloth folded on a table.
abstract.cn: 听布料在桌上被折起时的窸窣声。

abstract.en: See a bolt of blue cloth unrolled by a shopkeeper.
abstract.cn: 想象店主展开一匹蓝布。

examples.en: Cut the cloth along the red line.
examples.cn: 沿着红线裁布。

examples.en: She cleaned the blackboard with a dry cloth.
examples.cn: 她用干布擦了黑板。

examples.en: This town was famous for its fine cloth long ago.
examples.cn: 很久以前，这座小镇以精致的布料闻名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克罗斯」——布「洛」在手里软「丝丝」的，cloth 就是一匹柔软的布。

root: 日耳曼语 *klotham（来源不确定）→ 古英语 clath（布；衣物）→ 中古英语 cloth → 现代英语 cloth；同族词有德语 Tuch，派生词有 clothe（穿衣）、clothes（衣服）、clothing（服装总称）。

sensesIntro.en: Cloth stretches from a woven sheet to a wiping rag and a whole trade.
sensesIntro.cn: cloth 从织成的一幅布延伸到抹布和整个纺织业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat woven sheet, soft to the touch
core.cn: 核心意象：一幅摸上去柔软平整的织物

intro.en: Cloth fans out into the whole clothing family.
intro.cn: cloth 扩展出整个服装词族。

latinIntro.en: Cloth is Germanic, so its family is Germanic rather than Latin.
latinIntro.cn: cloth 属日耳曼词源，词族也是日耳曼而非拉丁的。

items.example: They clothed the children warmly.
items.exampleCN: 他们给孩子们穿得暖暖的。

items.example: Wash the clothes on Sunday.
The shop sells winter clothing.
The clothier opened a new shop.
This fabric never fades.
The textile factory moved away.

items.meaning: an old worn piece of cloth
items.example: He wiped the bike with a rag.
Pull the blanket over you.

definition_zh: 衣服；衣物
definition_en: things that you wear, such as shirts, dresses and trousers
core_image: 衣柜里挂着一排排要穿出门的衣裳
scene: 换季了，妈妈把衣柜里的厚衣服收进箱子。Wash the clothes and hang them to dry.
sceneCN: 这里 clothes 是「衣服」（第 1 个义项：穿在身上的衣物总称）；句意是把衣服洗好晾干。

pos.zh: 衣服；衣物（复数形式，无单数）

forms.label: 复数形式（本身即复数，无单数）

derivatives.zh: 由 cloth 加 -ing 构成，义为「服装（总称）」，语体较正式
与 clothes 同源，义为「壁橱」

senses.title: Things you wear
senses.definition: things such as shirts and trousers that people wear
senses.definitionCN: 衬衫、裤子这类人们穿戴的东西
senses.example: Put on your warm clothes before going out.
senses.exampleCN: 出门前穿上暖和的衣服。
senses.why: The word grew out of cloth, because garments are simply cloth cut and sewn for wearing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 cloth 生长而来，因为衣服不过是裁剪缝纫后的布。

senses.title: Bedding and household linen
senses.definition: bed sheets and covers, in the old sense
senses.definitionCN: 旧义中的床单与被盖
senses.example: Grandma aired the clothes in the spring sun.
senses.exampleCN: 奶奶在春日阳光下晒被褥。
senses.why: Older English counted sheets and blankets as clothes too, and country speech still remembers it.
senses.whyCN: 古英语把床单毯子也归入 clothes，乡下话里还留着这个影子。

intro.en: Clothes is cloth grown up: the same little word dressed itself into garments.
intro.cn: clothes 是长大了的 cloth：同一个小词为自己穿上了衣裳。

items.en: The base *klotham gave Old English clath, meaning cloth or covering.
items.cn: 词基 *klotham 给了古英语 clath，意为布或覆盖物。

items.en: Old English clathas was the plural, naming worn coverings.
items.cn: 古英语复数形式 clathas 指穿戴的覆盖物。

items.en: Middle English fixed clothes as the everyday plural for garments.
items.cn: 中古英语把 clothes 固定为衣物的日常说法。

items.en: Modern English kept clothes without a singular; one piece is simply an item of clothing.
items.cn: 现代英语的 clothes 没有单数形式，一件衣服要说 an item of clothing。

items.en: The sound softened over time: many speakers now say it like the word close plus z.
items.cn: 读音随时间弱化：许多人现在把它读成 close 加 z 的音。

note.en: The first group collects the cloth family; the second collects wear words.
note.cn: 第一组收 cloth 词族，第二组收穿戴类词。

entries.definition: Garments in general, more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「服装（总称）」，较正式。

entries.definition: Woven material.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「布料」，是 clothes 的源头词。

entries.definition: To shut or near.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或形容词，义为「关；近」，读音与 clothes 接近但词源不同。

entries.definition: One piece of clothing, formal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一件衣服」，语体正式。

entries.definition: A set of clothes worn together.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一套服装」。

entries.definition: Clothes, in a formal or literary way.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「服装」，正式或文学用语。

normalIntro.en: Remember clothes as cloth that learned to be worn.
normalIntro.cn: 把 clothes 记成「学会被穿」的 cloth。

normal.en: clothes is always plural; there is no single clothes.
normal.cn: clothes 永远是复数，没有单数形式。

normal.en: one piece is an item of clothing.
normal.cn: 一件衣服说 an item of clothing。

normal.en: clothes comes from the word cloth.
normal.cn: clothes 来自 cloth 一词。

normal.en: wash and hang clothes in the sun.
normal.cn: 在太阳下洗晒衣服。

normal.en: warm clothes keep the winter out.
normal.cn: 暖衣服挡住冬天。

abstract.en: See a wardrobe door swing open to rows of colors.
abstract.cn: 想象衣柜门打开，露出一排排颜色。

abstract.en: Feel a warm sweater swallowed straight from the dryer.
abstract.cn: 感受刚从烘干机取出的毛衣的暖意。

abstract.en: Hear the light flap of shirts drying in the wind.
abstract.cn: 听衬衫在风里晾晒时轻拍的响声。

examples.en: These clothes smell of sunshine after drying outside.
examples.cn: 在外面晒过的衣服有一股阳光味。

examples.en: Pack a change of clothes for the school trip.
examples.cn: 为学校郊游带一套换洗衣服。

examples.en: Old clothes were given to the village school.
examples.cn: 旧衣服送给了乡村学校。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克罗斯子」——衣柜里挂满衣裳，关上柜门「克罗斯」一声，clothes 就是那一柜衣裳。

root: 日耳曼语 *klotham → 古英语 clath（布）→ 复数 clathas（衣物）→ 中古英语 clothes → 现代英语 clothes（只作复数）；同源词有 cloth（布）、clothing（服装总称）。

sensesIntro.en: Clothes covers what you wear and, in older speech, bedding too.
sensesIntro.cn: clothes 涵盖穿的衣服，旧义还包括被褥。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cloth cut and sewn to be worn
core.cn: 核心意象：被裁剪缝纫、穿上身的布

intro.en: The clothes family keeps cloth at its heart.
intro.cn: clothes 词族的核心始终是 cloth。

latinIntro.en: Clothes is Germanic, so no Latin relative lives in this family.
latinIntro.cn: clothes 属日耳曼词源，家族中没有拉丁亲戚。

items.example: Sports clothing dries quickly.
The charity clothes poor children.
items.exampleCN: 慈善机构为贫困儿童提供衣物。

items.structure: old word of the cloth family
items.meaning: a small room for storing clothes
items.example: Hang your bag in the closet.
Each garment has a price tag.
She wore a red outfit to the party.
items.exampleCN: 她穿红色套装去参加聚会。

items.example: The wardrobe door squeaks.
Put the laundry in the basket.
Grandma's sewing saved the torn coat.
items.exampleCN: 奶奶的缝补救了破外套。

definition_zh: 服装；衣物（总称）
definition_en: garments in general; the things people wear considered as one group
core_image: 把所有人的衣裳装进一个大箱子，统称服装
scene: 冬季运动会前，体育老师提醒大家多带衣物。Warm clothing is needed for the winter camp.
sceneCN: 这里 clothing 是「服装（总称）」（第 1 个义项：衣服的整体概念，不可数）；句意是冬令营需要带保暖衣物。

derivatives.zh: 由 cloth 加 -e 构成，义为「给…穿衣」
与 clothing 同源，义为「衣服（复数形式）」

senses.title: Garments considered as a whole
senses.definition: all the garments people wear, treated as one uncountable group
senses.definitionCN: 人们穿的衣物被当作一个整体
senses.example: The shop sells sports clothing for children.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店卖儿童运动服装。
senses.why: Many separate shirts and coats can be gathered into one big idea, like water gathered into one river.
senses.whyCN: 一件件衬衫和大衣可以汇成一个整体概念，就像水汇成一条河。

senses.title: A covering that protects the body
senses.definition: a layer that covers and protects the body
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖并保护身体的层
senses.example: Firefighters wear special protective clothing.
senses.exampleCN: 消防员穿特殊的防护服。
senses.why: When cloth is worn for safety rather than style, the general word for garments still fits.
senses.whyCN: 当衣物是为了安全而非美观时，衣物的总称词依然适用。

intro.en: Clothing is cloth put to work, with a very old ending doing the job.
intro.cn: clothing 是被派上用场的 cloth，由一个古老的词缀来担当。

items.en: The base *klotham gave Old English clath, the bare word for cloth.
items.cn: 词基 *klotham 给了古英语 clath，即布的本词。

items.en: Old English already used clathing for garments as a whole.
items.cn: 古英语已用 clathing 指衣物的整体。

items.en: Middle English spelling varied, and the -ing form slowly won out.
items.cn: 中古英语拼法多样，-ing 形式逐渐胜出。

items.en: Modern English fixed clothing as the formal, uncountable word for garments.
items.cn: 现代英语把 clothing 定为不可数的正式说法。

items.en: Today clothing competes with clothes: clothes is casual, clothing is for shops and signs.
items.cn: 如今 clothing 与 clothes 并存：clothes 偏口语，clothing 用于店名与标签。

note.en: The first group collects the cloth family; the second collects garment words.
note.cn: 第一组收 cloth 词族，第二组收服装类词。

entries.definition: The things you wear, everyday plural.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「衣服」，与 clothing 同源，更口语。

entries.definition: Woven material.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「布料」，是词族的源头。

entries.definition: The act of coming to an end.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「结束」，拼写与 clothing 相近但词源不同。

entries.definition: One single piece of clothing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一件衣服」，可数。

entries.definition: Clothing, in formal or commercial style.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「服装」，正式或商业用语。

entries.definition: A suffix-like word for clothing types, as in footwear.
entries.definitionCN: 常作复合词后缀，如 footwear「鞋类」。

normalIntro.en: Remember clothing as the whole box of garments.
normalIntro.cn: 把 clothing 记成一整箱衣裳。

normal.en: clothing is uncountable: no clothing-s.
normal.cn: clothing 不可数，没有复数。

normal.en: one shirt is a piece of clothing.
normal.cn: 一件衬衫是 a piece of clothing。

normal.en: clothing sounds formal, clothes sounds casual.
normal.cn: clothing 偏正式，clothes 偏口语。

normal.en: protective clothing keeps workers safe.
normal.cn: protective clothing 保护工人安全。

normal.en: clothing comes from cloth plus -ing.
normal.cn: clothing 由 cloth 加 -ing 构成。

abstract.en: See one giant drawer holding every coat you own.
abstract.cn: 想象一个巨大抽屉装下你所有的大衣。

abstract.en: Feel a raincoat snap shut against the storm.
abstract.cn: 感受雨衣在风雨中扣紧。

abstract.en: Hear the hanger rack slide along in a big shop.
abstract.cn: 听大卖场里挂衣杆滑动的声音。

examples.en: Bring enough clothing for the five-day trip.
examples.cn: 为五天的旅行带够衣物。

examples.en: The old clothing was collected for recycling.
examples.cn: 旧衣物被集中回收。

examples.en: Lab workers must wear protective clothing.
examples.cn: 实验室人员必须穿防护服。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克洛星」——衣服多得像星星挂满衣柜，clothing 就是满天星星般的衣物总称。

root: 日耳曼语 *klotham → 古英语 clath（布）→ clathing（衣物总称）→ 中古英语 → 现代英语 clothing；同源词有 cloth（布）、clothes（衣服）、clothe（穿衣）。

sensesIntro.en: Clothing gathers garments into one whole and can also mean protective coverings.
sensesIntro.cn: clothing 把衣物汇成整体，也可指起保护作用的覆盖物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: all garments gathered into one big whole
core.cn: 核心意象：所有衣裳汇成的一个整体

branches.en: Cotton, wool and silk made wearable

intro.en: The -ing ending turns a small noun into a big collective idea.
intro.cn: -ing 词缀把小名词变成大的集合概念。

latinIntro.en: Clothing is Germanic, so Latin relatives are absent from this family.
latinIntro.cn: clothing 属日耳曼词源，家族中没有拉丁亲戚。

items.example: Fold your clothes neatly.
The program clothes hundreds of children.
items.exampleCN: 该项目为数百名儿童提供衣物。

items.example: Wrap the bowl in a cloth.
The garment is made of silk.
The store sells men's apparel.
The shop also sells footwear.
Pack light rainwear.
Clean underwear is packed.

definition_zh: 云；云朵；阴云；一大群；（网络）云端
definition_en: a white or grey mass of water drops floating in the sky
core_image: 天上飘着的一大团棉花，说变脸就变脸
scene: 操场上体育课，大家抬头看天上的大白云。Look at that big white cloud over the playground.
sceneCN: 这里 cloud 是「云朵」（第 1 个义项：天上飘浮的水汽团）；句意是看操场上空那朵大白云。

derivatives.zh: 由 cloud  + suffix  -y 构成，义为「多云的；阴天的」
由 cloud  + suffix  -less 构成，义为「无云的；晴朗的」
由 cloudy  + suffix  -ness 构成，义为「多云状态」

senses.title: A floating mass of water drops in the sky
senses.definition: a white or grey mass of tiny water drops in the sky
senses.definitionCN: 天空中由小水滴组成的白色或灰色团块
senses.example: A small cloud crossed the sun during the picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 野餐时一小朵云掠过太阳。
senses.why: Steam from the earth cools high above and gathers into something soft, heavy and visible.
senses.whyCN: 水汽升上高空冷却，聚成柔软、厚重、可见的一团。

senses.title: A mass of smoke, dust or flying things
senses.definition: a moving mass of smoke, dust or small flying insects
senses.definitionCN: 烟雾、尘土或飞虫形成的移动团块
senses.example: The car left a cloud of dust on the road.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车在路上扬起一团尘土。
senses.why: Anything that floats and hides the view behaves like sky-clouds, so the name flies down to earth.
senses.whyCN: 凡是飘浮遮挡视线的东西都像天上的云，这个名字便落到地上。

senses.title: Something that hides truth or spoils happiness
senses.definition: something that darkens a situation or a person's good name
senses.definitionCN: 使形势黯淡或名誉受损的事物
senses.example: The argument cast a cloud over the party.
senses.exampleCN: 争吵给聚会蒙上了阴影。
senses.why: Real clouds darken the sky; worries darken the mind, so the picture is borrowed for feelings.
senses.whyCN: 真的云遮蔽天空，忧愁遮蔽心情，画面便被借来形容情绪。

senses.title: To make something less clear
senses.definition: to make an idea, glass or memory less clear
senses.definitionCN: 让想法、玻璃或记忆变得模糊
senses.example: Tears clouded her eyes as she said goodbye.
senses.exampleCN: 道别时泪水模糊了她的双眼。
senses.why: A mist in front of the eyes works like a cloud in front of the sun.
senses.whyCN: 眼前的雾气就像太阳前的云。

intro.en: Cloud once meant something more solid than the sky: it began as a rock.
intro.cn: cloud 最初指比天空更坚实的东西：它起源于岩石。

items.en: Old English clud meant a mass of rock or a hill.
items.cn: 古英语 clud 指岩石堆或山丘。

items.en: People compared a big grey sky-mass to a pile of rocks, and the name transferred.
items.cn: 人们把灰白的大团云比作一堆岩石，名字随之转移。

items.en: By Middle English the sky sense had won completely and the rock sense was gone.
items.cn: 到中古英语，天空义完全获胜，岩石义消失。

items.en: Modern English kept cloud for sky masses, smoke and gloomy feelings.
items.cn: 现代英语用 cloud 指云、烟团和阴郁情绪。

items.en: In the internet age cloud was borrowed again for faraway computer storage.
items.cn: 互联网时代，cloud 又被借指远程计算机存储，即云端。

note.en: The first group collects the cloud family; the second collects sky words.
note.cn: 第一组收 cloud 词族，第二组收天空相关词。

entries.definition: Covered with many clouds.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多云的」，由 cloud 加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: Having no clouds at all.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「万里无云的」，由 cloud 加 -less 构成。

entries.definition: Influence or a heavy blow.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「影响力；重击」，拼写与 cloud 相近但词源不同。

entries.definition: Cloud that touches the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「雾」，是贴近地面的云。

entries.definition: Thin fog in the morning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「薄雾」，比 fog 更轻。

entries.definition: Dusty air that blurs the distance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「霾；雾霭」，使远处模糊。

normalIntro.en: Remember cloud through its rocky past and its modern home above computers.
normalIntro.cn: 从「岩石」的过去与电脑上方的现在记忆 cloud。

normal.en: cloud first meant a rock or hill.
normal.cn: cloud 最初指岩石或山丘。

normal.en: cloudy is cloud plus -y.
normal.cn: cloudy 是 cloud 加 -y。

normal.en: a cloud of dust rises behind cars.
normal.cn: 车后扬起 a cloud of dust。

normal.en: photos saved in the cloud live far away.
normal.cn: 存在云端的照片在很远的地方。

normal.en: under a cloud means being doubted.
normal.cn: under a cloud 指受到怀疑。

abstract.en: Lie on the grass and name the shapes in the drifting white.
abstract.cn: 躺在草地上给漂过的白云起名字。

abstract.en: Feel the cool grey blanket pressing before the rain.
abstract.cn: 感受雨前灰云压顶的清凉。

abstract.en: Watch a sad thought settle like fog over a sunny day.
abstract.cn: 看忧愁像雾一样罩住晴天。

examples.en: Dark clouds gathered, and we ran back to school.
examples.cn: 乌云聚拢，我们跑回了学校。

examples.en: The photos are saved in the cloud, not on this phone.
examples.cn: 照片存在云端，不在这部手机上。

examples.en: Smoke clouded the small kitchen while lunch burned.
examples.cn: 午饭烧糊时，烟雾弥漫了小厨房。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克劳德」——克劳德躺在草地上看云，cloud 就是他头顶那朵大白云。

root: 古英语 clud（岩石堆）→ 词义转移到灰白的天空大团 → 中古英语 cloud（云）→ 现代英语 cloud（云、烟团、阴影、云端）；派生词有 cloudy（多云的）、cloudless（无云的）。

sensesIntro.en: Cloud drifts from sky masses to smoke, shadows and even computer storage.
sensesIntro.cn: cloud 从天上的云团延伸到烟尘、阴影，甚至网络存储。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soft grey-white mass that floats and hides
core.cn: 核心意象：一团漂浮且遮蔽视线的灰白色软团

intro.en: Cloud builds weather words with simple English endings.
intro.cn: cloud 用简单的英语词缀构建天气词族。

latinIntro.en: Cloud is Germanic, so Latin lives only in borrowed science words like nimbus.
latinIntro.cn: cloud 属日耳曼词源，拉丁语只出现在借入的科学词如 nimbus 中。

items.example: It was cloudy on sports day.
A cloudless sky promised a good trip.
items.exampleCN: 万里无云预示旅途顺利。

items.example: The cloudiness lasted a whole week.
items.exampleCN: 多云天气持续了一整周。

items.example: Nimbus clouds bring heavy rain.
Fog covered the fields at dawn.
A mist rose from the river.
A summer haze hid the hills.
The sky was overcast all day.

definition_zh: 多云的；阴天的；浑浊的；模糊不清的
definition_en: covered with clouds; not clear or transparent
core_image: 天空被一层灰白棉被整个盖住
scene: 清晨出门，天色灰蒙蒙的像盖了被子。The weather report says it will be cloudy tomorrow.
sceneCN: 这里 cloudy 是「多云的；阴天的」（第 1 个义项：天空被云遮盖）；句意是天气预报说明天多云。

derivatives.zh: 由 cloudy 加后缀 -ness 构成，义为「多云；浑浊」
cloudy 的词源名词，义为「云」

senses.title: Covered with clouds
senses.definition: with many clouds in the sky
senses.definitionCN: 天空中有许多云
senses.example: It was cloudy all day, so we stayed indoors.
senses.exampleCN: 整天阴天，我们就待在室内。
senses.why: The sky loses its blue when the grey-white masses gather over it.
senses.whyCN: 灰白的云团聚拢，天空便失去了蓝色。

senses.title: Not transparent or clean
senses.definition: not clear, especially of liquids
senses.definitionCN: 液体不透明、不干净
senses.example: The river water looked cloudy after the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨后河水看起来很浑浊。
senses.why: Mud floating in water hides what is below, working like clouds in front of the sky.
senses.whyCN: 泥沙悬浮在水中遮住底部，就像云遮住天空。

senses.title: Not clear in the mind
senses.definition: uncertain or not remembered clearly
senses.definitionCN: 不确定或记忆不清
senses.example: My memory of that day is still cloudy.
senses.exampleCN: 我对那天的记忆仍很模糊。
senses.why: A mist over the eyes becomes a mist over the mind, and neither sees clearly.
senses.whyCN: 眼前的雾成了心中的雾，两者都看不清。

intro.en: Cloudy is cloud wearing an old adjective ending.
intro.cn: cloudy 是 cloud 戴上了古老的形容词词尾。

items.en: The base *kulo gave Old English col, charcoal, later mineral coal.
items.cn: 词基 *kulo 给了古英语 col（木炭），后来指矿物煤。

items.en: Old English clud, a rock mass, shifted to the grey sky mass.
items.cn: 古英语 clud 本指岩石团，转到灰白的天上大团。

items.en: The adjective ending -y turns nouns into adjectives, as in sun and sunny.
items.cn: 形容词后缀 -y 把名词变成形容词，如 sun 变 sunny。

items.en: Cloudy appeared in Modern English for skies full of clouds.
items.cn: 现代英语用 cloudy 形容满是云的天空。

items.en: Later cloudy widened to dirty water and dim memories.
items.cn: 后来 cloudy 又扩展到浑浊的水和模糊的记忆。

note.en: The first group collects the cloudy family; the second collects sky and clarity words.
note.cn: 第一组收 cloudy 词族，第二组收天空与清晰类词。

entries.definition: The state of being cloudy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「多云；浑浊」，由 cloudy 加 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: A white or grey sky mass.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「云」，是 cloudy 的词源名词。

entries.definition: Having no clouds at all.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无云的」，由 cloud 加 -less 构成。

entries.definition: Fully covered by clouds.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「阴云密布的」，比 cloudy 更浓。

entries.definition: Dark and hard to see through.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「昏暗的；浑浊的」。

entries.definition: Not clear or certain.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「模糊的」，与 cloudy 第 3 义项相近。

normalIntro.en: Remember cloudy as cloud with the little adjective tail -y.
normalIntro.cn: 把 cloudy 记成 cloud 加上小小的形容词尾巴 -y。

normal.en: cloudy is cloud plus -y.
normal.cn: cloudy 是 cloud 加 -y。

normal.en: cloudier and cloudiest are the comparing forms.
normal.cn: cloudier 和 cloudiest 是比较级和最高级。

normal.en: cloudy water cannot be seen through.
normal.cn: cloudy water 看不透。

normal.en: partly cloudy means some sun shows.
normal.cn: partly cloudy 指偶尔出太阳。

normal.en: cloudless is the opposite of cloudy.
normal.cn: cloudless 是 cloudy 的反义词。

abstract.en: See the whole sky wrapped in soft grey wool.
abstract.cn: 想象整个天空裹在柔软的灰羊毛里。

abstract.en: Stir muddy pond water and lose sight of the bottom.
abstract.cn: 搅动泥塘的水，看不见池底。

abstract.en: Reach for an old memory and touch only its edges.
abstract.cn: 伸手取一段旧记忆，却只碰到边缘。

examples.en: A cloudy sky followed us through the whole school trip.
examples.cn: 整个学校旅行都伴随着阴天。

examples.en: The tea turned cloudy when the milk mixed in.
examples.cn: 牛奶混进去后，茶变得浑浊。

examples.en: His cloudy answer left us guessing.
examples.cn: 他含糊的回答让我们只好猜测。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克劳迪」——天空「克劳」臃肿又灰「迪」，cloudy 就是盖满云的阴天。

root: cloud（云，源于古英语 clud 岩石团）+ 形容词后缀 -y → 现代英语 cloudy；派生词有 cloudiness（多云状态）、cloudless（无云的）。

sensesIntro.en: Cloudy starts with grey skies and muddies water and memories.
sensesIntro.cn: cloudy 从阴沉的天空延伸到浑浊的水与模糊的记忆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey blanket over the clear view
core.cn: 核心意象：盖住清晰景象的灰毯子

intro.en: The -y ending builds weather adjectives from everyday nouns.
intro.cn: -y 词尾把日常名词变成天气形容词。

latinIntro.en: Cloudy is Germanic, so Latin relatives are absent.
latinIntro.cn: cloudy 属日耳曼词源，没有拉丁亲戚。

items.example: A sunny morning woke the birds.
items.exampleCN: 晴朗的早晨唤醒了鸟儿。

items.example: Rainy weeks flooded the field.
A windy day is fine for kites.
The snowy road was quiet.
Foggy mornings slow the traffic.
items.exampleCN: 多雾的早晨让交通变慢。

items.example: The cloudiness lasted all week.
The overcast sky promised rain.
Murky water hid the stones.

definition_zh: 俱乐部；社团；棍棒；（纸牌）梅花
definition_en: a group of people who meet for an activity; a heavy stick
core_image: 一群人围着同一张桌子做同一件喜欢的事
scene: 周五下午，同学们在活动室里排练话剧。Tom joined the English club this term.
sceneCN: 这里 club 是「俱乐部；社团」（第 1 个义项：为共同爱好聚在一起的小团体）；句意是汤姆这学期加入了英语社团。

derivatives.zh: 由 club 加 house 构成，义为「俱乐部会所」
由 club 加 -ing 构成，义为「泡夜店」

senses.title: A group that meets for a shared activity
senses.definition: a group of people who meet regularly for a shared activity
senses.definitionCN: 为共同活动定期聚会的一群人
senses.example: Our chess club meets every Wednesday.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的国际象棋社团每周三活动。
senses.why: A heavy stick binds things together; a group binds people together, so the stick's name was given to the group.
senses.whyCN: 棍棒把东西捆在一起，社团把人聚在一起，棍棒的名字便给了社团。

senses.title: A heavy stick used as a weapon
senses.definition: a heavy stick used as a weapon or tool
senses.definitionCN: 用作武器或工具的粗棍
senses.example: The guard carried a long club.
senses.exampleCN: 保安带着一根长棍。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: a thick branch in the hand, heavy and solid.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：一根又粗又沉的树枝握在手里。

senses.title: One of the playing-card suits
senses.definition: one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards
senses.definitionCN: 扑克牌四种花色之一
senses.example: He played the ace of clubs and won the round.
senses.exampleCN: 他打出梅花尖子，赢了这一轮。
senses.why: French card makers used a leaf shape that English eyes read as a little club, and the name stayed.
senses.whyCN: 法国制牌人用三叶形，英国人看着像小棍棒，名字就留了下来。

senses.title: To hit with a stick
senses.definition: to hit someone or something with a heavy stick
senses.definitionCN: 用粗棍击打
senses.example: The farmers clubbed the snake to protect the hens.
senses.exampleCN: 农民用棍棒打蛇保护母鸡。
senses.why: When the stick is the tool, the tool's name becomes the action.
senses.whyCN: 当棍子成为工具，工具的名字就成了动作。

intro.en: Club began as a big solid stick and slowly became a group of solid friends.
intro.cn: club 起初是根粗棍棒，慢慢变成了一群铁哥们儿。

items.en: Old Norse klubba meant a heavy stick, and the word travelled with the Vikings.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 klubba 指粗棍棒，随维京人传入。

items.en: Middle English clubbe kept the weapon sense through the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语 clubbe 在十四世纪仍指武器。

items.en: People joked that a gathered group was a lump of people stuck together like a club.
items.cn: 人们打趣说聚在一起的人像被棍棒捆成的一坨，词义由此转指团体。

items.en: By the seventeenth century club firmly meant a society of members.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，club 已牢固指会员社团。

items.en: Later English added the card suit and the verb for hitting.
items.cn: 后来英语又添了梅花花色与击打的动词义。

note.en: The first group collects the club family; the second collects group words.
note.cn: 第一组收 club 词族，第二组收团体类词。

entries.definition: A building used by a club.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「俱乐部会所」，由 club 加 house 构成。

entries.definition: A hint that helps you solve something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「线索」，拼写与 club 相近但词源不同。

entries.definition: A young animal such as a lion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「幼兽」，与 club 字母相近，词源无关。

entries.definition: An organized group with shared interests.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「社团；协会」，较正式。

entries.definition: A formal group of members.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「协会」，正式用语。

entries.definition: A group working or playing together.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「队」，强调共同行动。

normalIntro.en: Remember club through its stick past and its member present.
normalIntro.cn: 从棍棒的过去与会员的现在记忆 club。

normal.en: club first meant a heavy stick.
normal.cn: club 最初指粗棍棒。

normal.en: a pack of cards has diamonds, hearts, spades and clubs.
normal.cn: 一副牌有方块、红桃、黑桃和梅花。

normal.en: join a club means become a member.
normal.cn: join a club 指成为会员。

normal.en: clubhouse is the club's own building.
normal.cn: clubhouse 是社团自己的房子。

normal.en: club together means join money or effort.
normal.cn: club together 指凑钱或合力。

abstract.en: Hear the shy knock at the club room door on a Friday.
abstract.cn: 想象周五活动室门口羞怯的敲门声。

abstract.en: Feel the heavy weight of a wooden stick in one hand.
abstract.cn: 感受单手握着木棍的沉重。

abstract.en: See a table of friends laughing over one board game.
abstract.cn: 想象一群朋友围着一张桌大笑。

examples.en: The singing club gave a show for the whole school.
examples.cn: 歌唱社团为全校办了一场演出。

examples.en: Keep a small club by the door when hiking in the hills.
examples.cn: 在山里徒步时，门口放根小棍棒以防万一。

examples.en: She sorted the hearts and the clubs into two piles.
examples.cn: 她把红桃和梅花分成两堆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克拉布」——社团聚会像螃蟹（crab）一样挤成一团，club 就是大家团在一起。

root: 古诺斯语 klubba（粗棍棒）→ 中古英语 clubbe（棍棒）→ 词义转指「聚成一团的人」→ 十七世纪定为「社团」→ 现代英语 club；派生词有 clubhouse（会所）、clubbing（泡夜店）。

sensesIntro.en: Club swings from a solid stick to a solid group, then to cards and blows.
sensesIntro.cn: club 从粗棍棒转到牢固的团体，再延伸到纸牌与击打。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: heavy things bound into one lump
core.cn: 核心意象：沉重之物被捆成一体

intro.en: Club grows compound words about membership and buildings.
intro.cn: club 构造了关于会员与会所的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Club is Norse in origin, so Latin relatives are absent.
latinIntro.cn: club 源自古诺斯语，没有拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: a building used by a club
items.example: We met in the clubhouse at four.
City students talk about clubbing.

items.meaning: a place open late for music
items.example: The night club plays loud music.

items.meaning: a group that reads and discusses books
items.example: Our book club reads one novel a month.
items.exampleCN: 我们的读书会每月读一本小说。

items.meaning: a formal group with shared aims
items.example: The science society meets on Monday.
She joined the students' association.
Our team won the relay race.
A gang of kids cleaned the park.

definition_zh: 教练；长途客车；辅导；（体育）训练
definition_en: a person who trains a team; a comfortable bus; to teach someone privately
core_image: 坐在场边，看着队伍一点点跑得更好的人
scene: 放学后的操场，老师拿着秒表喊加油。The coach asked us to run one more lap.
sceneCN: 这里 coach 是「教练」（第 1 个义项：训练队员的人）；句意是教练让我们再跑一圈。

derivatives.zh: 由 coach 加 -ing 构成，义为「辅导；训练」
由 coach 加 man 构成，义为「马车夫」

senses.title: A person who trains a team
senses.definition: a person who trains athletes or a team
senses.definitionCN: 训练运动员或球队的人
senses.example: Our coach taught us to pass before we shoot.
senses.exampleCN: 教练先教我们传球再射门。
senses.why: A coach once carried people along a fixed road; a trainer carries a team along a fixed plan, so the name moved over.
senses.whyCN: 马车沿固定路线载客前行，教练也沿固定计划带队伍，名字便移了过来。

senses.title: A comfortable long-distance bus
senses.definition: a large comfortable bus for long journeys
senses.definitionCN: 跑长途的大型舒适巴士
senses.example: We took the coach to Hangzhou for the school trip.
senses.exampleCN: 学校旅行我们坐大巴去杭州。
senses.why: The railway age turned the old horse carriage into a motor bus, keeping the old name.
senses.whyCN: 铁路时代把旧马车变成了大巴士，保留了旧名字。

senses.title: To teach someone privately
senses.definition: to teach a person or a small group one subject
senses.definitionCN: 一对一或小班教某科目
senses.example: Uncle Li coaches me in maths on Sundays.
senses.exampleCN: 李叔叔周日给我辅导数学。
senses.why: A tutor carries one student the way a carriage carried a few passengers, quietly and directly.
senses.whyCN: 家教像马车只载几位客人，安静而直接地把学生送往目标。

senses.title: A horse-drawn carriage
senses.definition: a closed carriage pulled by horses
senses.definitionCN: 马拉的封闭式车厢
senses.example: The old coach in the museum belongs to a king.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆里的老马车属于一位国王。
senses.why: This is the root sense: the covered box that rolled along the old roads.
senses.whyCN: 这是词源本义：沿旧路行驶的封闭车厢。

intro.en: Coach started in a Hungarian village and rolled across Europe on four wheels.
intro.cn: coach 起源于匈牙利的一个村庄，坐着四轮车驶遍了欧洲。

items.en: The name comes from Kocs, a Hungarian village famous for its carts.
items.cn: 此词源自以制车闻名的匈牙利村庄 Kocs。

items.en: French coche carried the carriage word into western Europe.
items.cn: 法语 coche 把「车厢」一词带进西欧。

items.en: Middle English coach meant the closed carriage drawn by horses.
items.cn: 中古英语 coach 指马拉的封闭式车厢。

items.en: People who carried students to exams were joked to be coaches, and the teacher sense was born.
items.cn: 人们打趣说帮学生突击应考的人像「载客马车」，教师义由此诞生。

items.en: Later the railway used coach for carriages, and the bus age kept it for long-distance coaches.
items.cn: 后来铁路把 coach 用于车厢，巴士时代又用它指长途客车。

note.en: The first group collects look-alike words; the second collects teaching and travel words.
note.cn: 第一组收形近词，第二组收教学与出行类词。

entries.definition: The act of teaching or training.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「辅导；训练」，由 coach 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: A person who drives a carriage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「马车夫」，由 coach 加 man 构成。

entries.definition: A long soft seat.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「长沙发」，拼写与 coach 仅一字母之差。

entries.definition: A person who trains athletes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「训练者」，与教练义近。

entries.definition: A private teacher for one student.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「家教」，强调一对一。

entries.definition: A big road vehicle for passengers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公交车」，coach 更舒适、跑长途。

normalIntro.en: Remember coach through its carriage road from village Kocs to the school field.
normalIntro.cn: 沿「从村庄 Kocs 到操场」的马车之路记忆 coach。

normal.en: coach comes from Kocs, a Hungarian village.
normal.cn: coach 来自匈牙利村庄 Kocs。

normal.en: coaches is the plural with -es.
normal.cn: 复数 coaches 以 -es 结尾。

normal.en: coach a team means train a team.
normal.cn: coach a team 指训练一支球队。

normal.en: take the coach means ride the long-distance bus.
normal.cn: take the coach 指坐长途大巴。

normal.en: coach and couch differ by one letter.
normal.cn: coach 与 couch 只差一个字母。

abstract.en: Hear the whistle cut the cold morning air on the field.
abstract.cn: 听哨声划破清晨操场的冷空气。

abstract.en: Feel the bus seat hum under you through the whole night road.
abstract.cn: 感受大巴座椅伴你整夜赶路的微微震动。

abstract.en: See the old carriage wheels turning in a museum photo.
abstract.cn: 想象博物馆照片里老马车的车轮。

examples.en: The coach clapped when we finally won the relay.
examples.cn: 我们终于赢了接力赛，教练鼓起掌来。

examples.en: The coach to Beijing leaves at seven tomorrow morning.
examples.cn: 去北京的大巴明早七点发车。

examples.en: Grandma showed us a photo of her coachman grandfather.
examples.cn: 奶奶给我们看了她马车夫祖父的照片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可驰」——马车「可驰」行千里，教练带你「可驰」向胜利，coach 就是那辆载你的车。

root: 匈牙利村庄 Kocs（以制车闻名）→ 法语 coche（车厢）→ 中古英语 coach（四轮马车）→ 喻指「载学生应考者」→ 现代英语「教练；长途客车」；派生词有 coaching（辅导）、coachman（马车夫）。

sensesIntro.en: Coach rolls from a Hungarian cart to buses, trainers and tutors.
sensesIntro.cn: coach 从匈牙利的车出发，滚向大巴士、教练与家教。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something that carries people along a set road
core.cn: 核心意象：沿既定道路载人前行之物

intro.en: Coach builds a family of wheels and teachers.
intro.cn: coach 繁衍出车轮与教师两支词族。

latinIntro.en: Coach is a place-name from Hungary, so Latin relatives are absent.
latinIntro.cn: coach 是匈牙利地名转来的，没有拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: the act of training or tutoring
items.example: Coaching helped her pass the test.

items.meaning: a driver of a horse carriage
items.example: The coachman wore a tall hat.

items.meaning: a place where coaches start and stop
items.example: The coach station was crowded at noon.
items.exampleCN: 中午的长途汽车站很拥挤。

items.example: The cat sleeps on the couch.
The trainer counts every push-up.
items.exampleCN: 训练者数着每一个俯卧撑。

items.example: His tutor explains sums slowly.

items.meaning: a person who teaches a skill
items.example: The instructor showed us the safe way.

items.meaning: a wheeled vehicle, railway or horse
items.example: First class carriage is at the front.

definition_zh: 煤；煤块；木炭
definition_en: a hard black substance dug from the ground and burned as fuel
core_image: 炉子里烧得通红的黑石块
scene: 冬天，爷爷往炉子里添了两块黑黑的燃料。Grandpa put more coal into the stove last night.
sceneCN: 这里 coal 是「煤；煤块」（第 1 个义项：可燃烧的黑色矿物）；句意是爷爷昨晚往炉子里添了些煤。

derivatives.zh: 由 char 加 coal 构成，义为「木炭」
由 coal 加 field 构成，义为「煤田」

senses.title: The black mineral fuel
senses.definition: a hard black substance dug from the earth and burned for heat
senses.definitionCN: 从地下挖出、可燃烧取热的黑色硬矿物
senses.example: This city once lived on coal mines.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市曾靠煤矿为生。
senses.why: Dug from the dark earth and burned in the dark stove, the black stone keeps houses warm.
senses.whyCN: 从黑暗的地底挖出，在黑暗的炉膛里燃烧，黑色的石头温暖了房屋。

senses.title: A single burning piece
senses.definition: one piece of coal, especially one that is burning
senses.definitionCN: 一块煤，尤指烧红的那块
senses.example: A red coal popped in the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 一块烧红的煤在火里噼啪作响。
senses.why: The mass becomes countable when each glowing piece can be seen and moved.
senses.whyCN: 当每块发亮的煤都看得见、搬得动时，整体便成了可数之物。

senses.title: Charcoal made from wood
senses.definition: black material made by burning wood slowly
senses.definitionCN: 木头缓慢烧成的黑色燃料
senses.example: Artists drew with sticks of coal.
senses.exampleCN: 画家用炭条画画。
senses.why: Older English counted wood charcoal under the same name, and drawing still remembers it.
senses.whyCN: 旧英语把木炭也归入此名，绘画用语里还留有痕迹。

intro.en: Coal is an old fire word: people have named it since they first fed stoves.
intro.cn: coal 是个古老的火词：自人类第一次给炉子添柴起便有了称呼。

items.en: The Germanic base *kulo meant something burned or charred.
items.cn: 日耳曼词基 *kulo 指被烧过或烧焦之物。

items.en: Old English col first meant charcoal, the burnt wood.
items.cn: 古英语 col 最初指木炭，即烧过的木头。

items.en: When mined stone fuel spread, Middle English gave the name to mineral coal.
items.cn: 当开采的石头燃料普及，中古英语把这名字给了矿物煤。

items.en: Modern English coal means the mined fuel; the wood fuel became charcoal.
items.cn: 现代英语 coal 指开采的煤；木头燃料改称 charcoal。

items.en: Industrial English added coalfield, coal mine and coal fire.
items.cn: 工业时代的英语又添了 coalfield、coal mine、coal fire 等词。

note.en: The first group collects the coal family; the second collects fuel words.
note.cn: 第一组收 coal 词族，第二组收燃料类词。

entries.definition: Black fuel or drawing material made from wood.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「木炭；炭笔」，由 char 加 coal 构成。

entries.definition: An area where coal is mined.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「煤田」，由 coal 加 field 构成。

entries.definition: A little cold.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「凉的」，拼写与 coal 仅一字母之差。

entries.definition: Wood burned slowly into black fuel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「木炭」，由木头烧成。

entries.definition: Any material burned for energy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「燃料」，范围更广。

entries.definition: Fuels made by heating coal without air.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「焦炭」，由煤加工而成。

normalIntro.en: Remember coal through the glowing stove and the old charcoal fire.
normalIntro.cn: 借发亮的炉子与古老的炭火记忆 coal。

normal.en: coal is dug from the ground as a black stone.
normal.cn: coal 是从地下挖出的黑色石头。

normal.en: charcoal is wood coal, not mineral coal.
normal.cn: charcoal 是木炭，不是矿物煤。

normal.en: a coal mine is a place that digs coal.
normal.cn: coal mine 指煤矿。

normal.en: carry coals to Newcastle means doing something useless.
normal.cn: carry coals to Newcastle 指多此一举。

normal.en: red coals glow in a winter fire.
normal.cn: 冬天的炉火里红煤发亮。

abstract.en: Feel the warm bricks near the kitchen stove in January.
abstract.cn: 感受一月里厨房炉边的暖砖。

abstract.en: See red light breathe inside the black stone.
abstract.cn: 想象黑石里透出的呼吸般的红光。

abstract.en: Hear the soft pop of a settling fire at night.
abstract.cn: 听夜里炉火安睡时轻轻的一声爆响。

examples.en: The old train burned coal and blew white smoke.
examples.cn: 老式火车烧煤，喷出白烟。

examples.en: She drew the mountain with a stick of charcoal.
examples.cn: 她用炭条画了一座山。

examples.en: Miners came up from the coal mine with black faces.
examples.cn: 矿工们满脸乌黑地从煤矿里上来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「寇尔」——炉火一旺，「寇」敌千军，coal 就是那把冬天烧得通红的黑石头。

root: 日耳曼语 *kulo（烧焦之物）→ 古英语 col（木炭）→ 中古英语转指矿物煤 → 现代英语 coal（煤）；同族词有德语 Kohle，派生词有 charcoal（木炭）、coalfield（煤田）。

sensesIntro.en: Coal moves from the mined fuel to single glowing pieces and old charcoal.
sensesIntro.cn: coal 从开采的煤延伸到烧红的煤块和旧义的木炭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: black stone that holds hidden fire
core.cn: 核心意象：藏着火的黑色石头

intro.en: Coal combines into compounds of mining and burning.
intro.cn: coal 与 mining、burning 相关词组合成复合词。

latinIntro.en: Coal is Germanic, so Latin relatives are absent from this family.
latinIntro.cn: coal 属日耳曼词源，家族中没有拉丁亲戚。

items.example: We grilled fish over charcoal.
The coalfield employed thousands.

items.meaning: a place where coal is dug
items.example: The coal mine closed last year.
Steel works burn coke.
Gas is a clean fuel.

items.meaning: a glowing piece in a fire
items.example: The embers kept the room warm all night.

items.meaning: a substance dug from the earth
